headline: Integrating multi-source evidence to prioritize genes for disease and metabolic discovery
label: Computational Gene Prioritization Resources
summary: Recent preprints combine network prediction, LLM literature mining, and co-essentiality mapping to prioritize genes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational gene prioritization from integrated evidence rather than single-source association. The rare disease study applies a network-based algorithm to predict novel genes across more than 200 rare diseases and supplies a gene-disease specificity score for variant prioritization. DDH integrates gene dependency, expression, and literature data for about 20,000 human genes using pathway co-essentiality mapping. thematicGO and GeneReL address adjacent needs: thematicGO condenses Gene Ontology enrichment output into biological themes via keyword matching and score aggregation, while GeneReL uses an LLM to extract Arabidopsis regulatory relationships from literature with a five-step gene normalization pipeline. What is new is the emphasis on structured relationships, namely co-essentiality across pathways and specificity scores tied to variants. Only the rare disease work addresses variant-level assessment directly.
